title: Idempotents extend across a flat uniformizer localization
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative domain, $\pi\in R$ an irreducible element, and $B$ a commutative $R$-algebra which is flat as an $R$-module [def-weil-flat-ring-map]. Assume $B/\pi B$ is reduced. For every idempotent $e\in B[1/\pi]$, there exists $b\in B$ whose image under the localization map is $e$.

source.place: Tag 055J, proof, affine fibre and denominator calculation

proof.text: Flatness over the domain makes multiplication by pi, and hence every power of pi, injective. Therefore B maps injectively into B[1/pi]. Write e=b/pi^n and induct on n.

When n=0 the numerator is the desired lift. For n+1, idempotence and injectivity imply b squared equals pi^(n+1) times b. Modulo pi this numerator has square zero, hence vanishes by reducedness. Write b=pi c, cancel the unit pi after localization, and apply the induction hypothesis to c.
